title: Latency & cost surface simulator for kernel combination scoring
creator: Priya Singh
description: Build a deterministic simulator that models the joint latency and token-cost surface for combinations of execution kernels across prefill and decode phases. The tool will be used by the autotuner to quickly evaluate candidate kernel portfolios for specific HW profiles and observed sequence-length distributions without running full-scale microbenchmarks on every change.
background: Current autotuning iterates by running many microbenchmarks on real hardware which is slow and noisy. We need a middle ground: a calibrated analytical + empirical simulator that predicts latency/cost for kernel chains (e.g., fused attention implementation A + matmul kernel B during prefill, different decode kernel during streaming) given model dims, batch, seqlen distribution, and GPU characteristics. This speeds up optimizer search and reduces the number of live GPU experiments required.
goals: Produce a simulator with median latency prediction error < 8% and 95th percentile error < 15% across a set of 6 target GPUs and 4 canonical model families
Integrate simulator outputs into the autotuner scoring function so candidate kernel portfolios with predicted better latency/cost are prioritized for hardware verification
Expose a lightweight CLI and internal HTTP endpoint for the runtime and CI to call during model onboarding and PR checks
non_goals: Replacing all hardware microbenchmarks (simulator will reduce but not eliminate them)
Modeling low-level thermal throttling dynamics or long-term drift (out of scope for this iteration)
acceptance_criteria: Simulator repo with unit tests and integration tests committed to internal monorepo
Calibration pipeline that uses an existing microbenchmark corpus to fit model parameters for each supported GPU type
Autotuner uses simulator scoring in the default candidate ranking path behind a feature flag
Benchmark report comparing simulator predictions vs real microbenchmarks for 6 GPUs and 4 model families included in the PR
design_notes: Hybrid approach: analytic cost model (FLOP/byte estimates) + empirically-fitted kernel latency offsets and bandwidth ceilings
Represent kernel combos as directed sequences with resource overlap allowances (e.g., overlap of prefill matmul with attention KV cache writes)
Sequence-length distribution inputs: accept histogram or parametric (mean+tail) format used by runtime telemetry
Uncertainty quantification: produce mean/CI to guide conservative rollback thresholds
implementation_plan: Week 1: scaffold simulator service and schema for kernel combo descriptions + implement simple analytic cost functions
Week 2: add calibration harness to ingest microbenchmark dataset and fit per-kernel offsets; implement GPU profile descriptor format
Week 3: integrate seqlen-distribution sampling, add prefill/decode phase modeling and overlap rules
Week 4: expose HTTP endpoint + CLI; add integration tests and run calibration on 6 GPUs
Week 5: wire into autotuner ranking path behind feature flag; run A/B runs to measure reduction in microbenchmark count during autotune
experiments: Compare pure analytic model vs hybrid (analytic+fitted) on prediction error
Evaluate impact of using histogram vs parametric seqlen input on prediction quality
Measure autotuner convergence time (wall-clock) when using simulator ranking vs baseline brute-force microbenchmarking
benchmarks_to_run: 4 model families: small-transformer (seq512), medium-LLM (seq1024), long-context (seq4096), decoder-only chat (prefill 512 decode 512)
Metrics: median latency per token, tail latency (95th), end-to-end prefill latency, GPU utilization, predicted vs observed token-cost
tradeoffs: Simulator complexity vs maintainability: more detailed models reduce error but increase maintenance burden as kernels evolve
Calibration frequency: frequent recalibration improves accuracy but requires access to GPUs and time; choose monthly baseline with on-demand recalibrate for new kernels
Conservative scoring may bias toward known kernels and slow exploration — mitigate with controlled exploration budget in autotuner
risks: Simulator underestimates tail behavior leading to SLO misses when deployed; mitigated by conservative CI and required hardware verification step
Kernel implementation changes (e.g., new fused attention) invalidating fitted parameters; mitigate by tying calibration to CI and kernel release process
Mismatch between telemetry seqlen histograms and synthetic inputs; mitigate by adding telemetry ingestion and example export in PR checks
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal runtime team only. Run simulator-driven autotune jobs for 10 model-onboardings, collect metrics
Beta: enable for Dedicated customers in sandbox region behind feature flag and opt-in TTL
GA: simulator becomes default ranking heuristic with mandatory hardware verification step before final commit to model profile
observability: Endpoint logs with input kernel combos and predicted latency/cost surface
Calibration dashboard showing per-kernel residuals across GPUs
Autotuner telemetry: # of candidate portfolios skipped due to simulator, final validation pass counts
